### Scaled coefficient and power results

Write \(mathcal E=(|w|, |r|, |e^{-z}-1|, |e^z-1|)\). A “scaled coefficient” \(C\) means \(mathcal E\le(C/L^2,C/L^3,C/L^3,C/L^3)\) componentwise on the whole stated ray. The strongest displayed rows for a given assumption are always used together with **all** eligible original and inherited alternatives. From the new density-mode tables:

| inclusive log onset | 170 | 180 | 190 | 200 | 220 | 240 | 300 | 400 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| matched B0 | \(3.756\cdot10^{-8}\) | \(3.756\cdot10^{-8}\) | \(3.448\cdot10^{-8}\) | \(1.048\cdot10^{-8}\) | \(9.698\cdot10^{-10}\) | \(8.963\cdot10^{-11}\) | \(6.926\cdot10^{-14}\) | \(4.150\cdot10^{-19}\) |
| with D02 | \(2.632\cdot10^{-8}\) | \(5.813\cdot10^{-9}\) | \(1.289\cdot10^{-9}\) | \(2.862\cdot10^{-10}\) | \(1.415\cdot10^{-11}\) | \(6.992\cdot10^{-13}\) | \(8.269\cdot10^{-17}\) | \(2.173\cdot10^{-23}\) |

At fixed scale coefficient \(10^{-8},10^{-10},10^{-12},10^{-18}\), one may respectively use log onsets \(176.39,206.99,237.62,329.20\) with D02 versus \(200.38,239.07,277.67,392.71\) with the matched B0 density construction. Further starts including the powers in the following paragraph are in d02_coeff.txt. The corresponding **table-free** comparison is in d02_basic_mid.txt; for example at \(L=230\) the new coefficient is \(9.727\cdot10^{-10}\), versus \(5.771\cdot10^{-8}\) in the B0 basic calculation. These are sufficient bounds, not minimal coefficients or starts.
rows.source_original_assumptions_preserved: B0 + exact D02 (published density corollary/table trust)

actual_readback.bytes:
For robustness independently of the density table, for \(L\ge300\)
one has the same errors bounded by \(.0626 Lx^{-a}\) and
\(.0626 L^2 x^{-a}\), respectively, under the same two exponents.
This uses S1 and S8 only. It is weaker than the main portfolio
but still transmits the new power.

rows.exact_statement: Density-free C=0.0626/0.0626 in B0/B1 for products and recips (multiply L x^-a) and weighted (multiply L^2 x^-a).

coefficient, e.g. \(.002\,x^{-1/8}/L\) and \(.002\,x^{-1/8}\)
from 170, already using the 170 power row and the decreasing
ratio \(e^{-L/32}\). The matched old density floor alone
prevents such a coefficient on any whole ray within this

rows.exact_statement: B1 gives coefficient .002 in the old 1/8 exponent units with same log powers, and the shown B0 envelope cannot certify that constant on a whole ray.
rows.full_domain: L>=170 closed; latter statement pertains to asymptotic envelope floor.

actual_readback.bytes: The continuous-coefficient formula in §5 is stronger than rounding these tables, and the signed pointwise interval formula in §6 can be still stronger. At the common onset 200 the ratio of the \(B_1\) to \(B_0\) displayed power radii is \((.226/.0135)\exp(-L/32)<.033\), decreasing thereafter. Against the enumerated pointwise original-input envelope (including the \(B_0\) signed and ordinary spectral transfers), the D02 bound is strictly smaller throughout \(L\ge200\); see the guard proof in §6. More generally, between any two displayed power rows of different exponent the crossover is exactly \(L=32\log(C_1/C_0)\) if it is in the matched domain; do not compare where a branch is inapplicable. For example, a target radius of \(10^{-14}\) for \(L|\mathcal P-1|,L|\mathcal Q-1|,L|E_1|,|E_w|\) is certified from \(L=224\) by a displayed \(B_0\) row and from \(L=198\) by a \(B_1\) row. For target \(10^{-18}\) the respective choices are 296 and 255. These examples give sufficient onsets, not lower bounds on other possible methods.

rows.exact_statement: Scaled all-output targets 1e-14 from 224/198, and 1e-18 from 296/255 for B0/B1, supported by submitted fallback rows.
rows.full_domain: Each inclusive real ray from its respective log onset
